response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT archstat, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scanqc GROUP BY archstat), s AS (SELECT archstat, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT s.archstat, s.cnt AS record_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_above_average FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC;

assumptions.assumption: A missing status means archstat IS NULL. GROUP BY puts all NULLs in one group, which is reported with a NULL status. Empty strings or other placeholder text are treated as ordinary distinct statuses.
The average share is the mean of the per-status shares, which equals 1 divided by the number of distinct statuses (including the NULL group). It is not a per-record average.
Every row in scanqc is one QC record, so the count is COUNT(*). Shares and differences are left as unrounded floating-point values.
